chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Is intercourse disliked during a specific time among the times, even if it is permissible?' He said, 'Yes. Between the emergence of dawn and the emergence of the sun, and from the setting of the sun to the disappearance of the redness (shafaq), and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed, and on the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the night and the day in which there is the black wind, the red wind, and the yellow wind, and the day and the night in which there is an earthquake.'

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spent the night with one of his wives during a night in which the moon was eclipsed. So there did not occur from him during that night what usually occurred from him during other nights, until he morninged. So she said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Is it due to hatred from you during this night?' He said, 'No, but this sign appeared during this night, so I disliked that I should delight and be engrossed therein. And Allah has rebuked a people, so the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book: "If they see a fragment of the sky falling, they will say: Piled up clouds." So leave them until they meet their day on which they will be thunderstruck.'

Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'And I swear by Allah, whoever has intercourse during these times which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade, and the news has reached him, will be granted a child, but he will see in that child what he does not like.'

key_terms.آية: Sign or verse (contextually referring to a divine sign/event)
key_terms.الشفق: The redness in the sky after sunset or before sunrise
key_terms.الكسوف: Eclipse (specifically of the sun or moon)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times when sexual intercourse is considered disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) delineates specific times of 'krah' (dislikability) for marital intimacy, linking them to cosmic phenomena like eclipses and earthquakes, which serve as divine signs. The narration highlights the Prophet’s voluntary abstention during a lunar eclipse to avoid distraction from contemplation, illustrating a balance between permissible acts and spiritual mindfulness. This tradition underscores the Shia scholarly view that such timings are not strictly forbidden but are discouraged to preserve the sanctity of the act and potentially influence the character of offspring.
